使用 CV 仍可能過度調參或洩漏資料。

stem: Which statements about validation cost and stability are generally correct? Select all that apply.
options: Cross-validation reduces reliance on a single train/test partition.
One train/test partition costs more fitting than k-fold validation.
Repeated cross-validation needs more fits than one k-fold run.
Repeated cross-validation inherently makes estimates less stable.

stem: You select the most variable features using the full dataset, then run CV. What is the main assessment concern?
options: Validation becomes redundant after a feature subset is selected.
Validation folds influenced the feature choice before evaluation.
Feature removal guarantees the fitted model will be underfit.
Selection makes any resulting validation error negligible.
explanations: 選特徵之後仍需估計泛化表現。
應把選特徵放在每折訓練資料內，避免驗證資料影響建模流程。
移除特徵不一定造成欠擬合。
選特徵不保證改善準確度，也不消除評估偏差。

I first perform feature selection on the entire dataset by selecting the most variable features. I then
evaluate model performance using cross-validation on these selected features. What is the main issue

You are introducing data leakage because feature selection should be performed within each cross-validation fold.

stem: Which options best describe bootstrap resampling? Select all that apply.
options: The same observations with their outcome labels reassigned.
The same observations each appearing once in a new order.
A resample in which some observations appear repeatedly.
A resample in which some original observations are absent.
explanations: Bootstrap 重抽整筆資料，不是任意打亂標籤與特徵配對。
一般 bootstrap 不是刻意將每筆恰取一次；但偶然全部恰取一次的結果確實可能。
有放回抽樣通常產生重複觀察值。
有些原始觀察值通常未被抽中，形成 out-of-bag 資料。
note: PDF 建議 C、D，但原題若問「可能出現」則 B 也可能；且 C、D 並非每次必然發生。保留來源爭議，此題不納入分數。
originalStem:
Which of the following options best describes a dataset obtained through bootstrap resampling? /
Select all that apply.
originalOptions: The original sample, with labels shuffled around.
The original sample in a different order.
The original sample with certain observations appearing more than once.
The original sample without certain observations.

stem: Cats are the majority class and the classifier predicts only cats. Which changes address the imbalance or its evaluation? Select all that apply.

Report an F1 score focused on minority-class detection.
Reduce dimensions without changing sampling or evaluation.
Select features using only the minority-class dog images.

all that apply.

Use a different metric, such as F1 score.
Perform dimension reduction.
Use feature selection on the dog images.

stem: A 95/5 classification dataset is mean-imputed and SMOTE-balanced before the 80/20 split. What is the main concern?

Pre-split processing can leak information and inflate evaluation.
The test set necessarily preserves the original class prevalence.
Minority-class bias must increase in every future population.
explanations: 沒有必然的欠擬合結論；主要問題是切分順序。

未來偏差方向無法由這些操作直接斷言。

Impute missing values using the mean of the full dataset
Apply SMOTE to balance the classes
Then perform an 80/20 train–test split
Which issue is most likely to occur?
originalOptions: The model will underfit because SMOTE increases variance
Data leakage leading to overly optimistic performance estimates
Reduced impact of class imbalance in the test set
Increased bias toward the minority class in real-world data

stem: Which pipeline best avoids leakage in fraud detection with missing values and class imbalance?
options: Impute the full dataset, balance classes, then split for evaluation.
Split the dataset, balance both sets, then estimate imputation rules.
Split the dataset, fit train-only imputation, then balance training only.
Balance the full dataset, remove missing rows, then cross-validate.
explanations: 全資料插補及平衡發生在切分前，會污染評估。
測試集應保留目標族群分布，不能一起平衡來報正式表現。
訓練資料學習插補規則，套用至測試；只平衡訓練部分。
切分前平衡仍有洩漏；CV 不能補救已發生的資訊使用。
originalStem:
In a fraud detection problem with severe class imbalance, you notice missing values in several
predictors. Which pipeline best avoids data leakage while addressing missing values and imbalance
correctly?
originalOptions: Impute missing values on the full dataset → balance classes → split data
Split data → balance classes on both sets → impute missing values
Split data → impute missing values using training data → balance only the training set
Balance classes first → remove missing values → cross-validate
